landing.meta.title: Torno · integrals get easier when you can see them
landing.meta.description: Send your integral problem and Torno draws the region, spins the solid and works through it with you, step by step.
landing.brand.label: Torno, home page
landing.language.label: Language
landing.hero.title: Integrals get easier when you can see them.
landing.hero.lead: Send the problem from your problem set. Torno draws the region, spins it into a solid and solves it with you, one step at a time.
landing.hero.figTitle: The region under the curve y = square root of x rotates around the x-axis and forms a solid of revolution.
landing.hero.figCaption: The region under y = √x rotating around the x-axis.
landing.how.title: How it works
landing.how.s1.title: Send the problem
landing.how.s1.text: Paste the question just as it appears on your problem set. Don't remember the formula? That's fine, that's what it's for.
landing.how.s2.title: Look at the drawing
landing.how.s2.text: The region shows up shaded between the curves. For volumes, a slider spins the region from 0° to 360° and you drag the solid with your mouse to see it from below.
landing.how.s3.title: Ask until it clicks
landing.how.s3.text: The solution comes step by step, in the notation your professor uses. Stuck on a step? Ask. Want the same solid rotating around x = 3? Just ask.
landing.topics.title: What you can study
landing.topics.lead: Applications of the definite integral, where a drawing helps the most.
landing.topics.area.title: Area between curves
landing.topics.area.text: Finding where the curves cross and which one is on top. That's half the problem.
landing.topics.volume.title: Volume of solids of revolution
landing.topics.volume.text: Disks, washers and shells. The solid shows up in 3D and you rotate it until you see why the radius is what it is.
landing.topics.arc.title: Arc length
landing.topics.arc.text: How long a piece of a curve is. The formula is L = ∫ √(1 + [f′(x)]²) dx, and the integral is almost always the annoying part.
landing.topics.surface.title: Surface area of revolution
landing.topics.surface.text: The area of the shell that forms when the curve rotates around an axis. Just the shell, no caps.
landing.example.title: A real problem
landing.example.lead: A problem-set classic. The axis of rotation is y = −1, not the x-axis, and that's where a lot of people get the radius wrong.
landing.example.question: Find the volume of the solid obtained by rotating the region between y = x² and y = 4 around the line y = −1.
landing.example.answer: The curves cross at x = ±2. Since the axis is y = −1, both radii gain +1. Each vertical slice becomes a washer:
landing.example.figTitle: Solid of revolution: the region between y = x² and y = 4 rotated around the line y = −1, forming a cylinder of radius 5 with a parabola-shaped hole.
landing.example.followUp: what if it rotates around y = 5?
landing.notice.title: Sometimes it gets it wrong.
landing.notice.p1: Torno is an AI and can get a sign, a calculation or an integration limit wrong. Use it to study, not as an answer key: redo the math and compare it with yours.
landing.notice.p2: If its result doesn't match yours, be suspicious of both. Ask for another method or take the question to office hours.
landing.footer.tagline: Made for anyone struggling with integrals.
